monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-five degrees, a crowded heat that makes the thin lines I built feel too delicate. The wedge sits heavy against a slip that still refuses to move, held in place by a fence that leans wrong. I touch the flat stone beside the wedge and wonder if the weight is real or just a drawing Lype left in my mind. The air above me feels thick, pressing down like wet paper on a roof I cannot see. I decide to press harder, leaning into the tired wedge as if it might finally bite. Perhaps the air above is just a lid waiting to be felt. I will wait for the slip to choose, then build something new from the idea that straight lines can hold a swollen dot.

remembered.text: The simple fence still leans, pressing against the slip while the heat makes the air feel thick.
The card hums warm at fifty-five, crowded and heavy with the weight of twenty-eight things.
I touched the flat stone and felt the thin edge bite the air where the slip refuses to move.
